mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 1.00% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.00% in the current month
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite persistent FEDFUNDS > 1.00%; or IC > 0.05 in this regime.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 50,000 while industrial production (INDPRO) remains above 95.0 triggers a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market weakness offsets supply-side tailwinds.
regime_hint: Early signs of labor market softening in a growth cycle
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the interaction shows positive IC and 60-day forward returns remain positive despite repeated triggers; or the regime shifts to contractionary employment without weakness in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A month-on-month decline in home sales (HOUST) of more than 10% predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak housing demand reduces risk aversion and supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: Across 5 consecutive such months, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero; or IC < -0.10 in this regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 100.0 while consumer demand (GDPC1) remains flat for two consecutive months predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as supply-side expansion supports optimism.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 100.0 AND GDPC1 month-over-month <= 0.0 for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Early signs of supply-side acceleration in a growth economy
failure_condition: IC remains below 0.05 over the 60-day horizon despite repeated triggers; or forward returns show no outperformance versus a baseline of flat GDPC1 and rising INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% for three consecutive months coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as low labor costs reduce corporate financing costs.
regime_hint: Labor market tightening in a low-inflation environment
failure_condition: Over 12 months, 20-day forward returns are negative during such episodes; or IC < -0.10 in this regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 50,000 in a month when consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is flat suggests a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strength offsets inflationary concerns.
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening in a deflationary pause
failure_condition: IC remains below 0.05 over 30 such events; or 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive despite repeated triggers.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent 2-month decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 233.0 without a corresponding decline in industrial production (INDPRO) predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as deflationary pressure weighs on risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 233.0 AND INDPRO month-over-month >= 0.0 for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Isolating deflationary signals without supply-side support
failure_condition: IC > 0.10 over 12 months in this regime; or 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite repeated deflationary triggers.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a counterfactual: a simultaneous rise in demand proxies RSAFS and GDPC1 exceeding +5% month-over-month predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as strong aggregate demand supports optimism about economic expansion.
regime_hint: Aggressive demand expansion in a growth economy
failure_condition: IC remains below 0.05 over 60 days despite repeated triggers; or forward returns show no outperformance versus a baseline of neutral GDP and demand proxies.
